s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of psychotic symptoms with hallucinations and delusions in a previously healthy individual
salient_findings: Episodes of talkativeness, incoherent speech, visual and auditory hallucinations
Elevated γ‐glutamyl transferase and total bilirubin
Positive COVID-19 antigen test and confirmatory RT-PCR
key_facts: 35-year-old West African man
No prior psychiatric or medical history
1-week history of escalating behavioral changes
Family reported episodes of talkativeness, incoherent speech, visual and auditory hallucinations
Denies head injury, substance use, or stressors
No family history of psychiatric illness
Potential mercury exposure through work in a mining community
Afebrile, BP 135/80 mmHg, pulse 88 bpm
Normal respiratory rate and oxygen saturation
General and neurologic exams were unremarkable
Appeared disheveled, restless, and agitated
Speech was loud and clear without latency
Exhibited circumstantial thought, grandiose delusions, and persecutory delusions
Both auditory and visual hallucinations
Memory was intact and he had no insight
Normal CBC, renal function, and albumin
Elevated γ‐glutamyl transferase at 81 IU/L
Total bilirubin 26 μmol/L
Malaria and typhoid screens were negative
Urinalysis revealed transient proteinuria and glycosuria
Head CT scan was normal

shortlist.label: COVID-19-Associated Psychosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient is COVID-19 positive and presents with acute onset of psychotic symptoms

shortlist.label: Mercury Poisoning
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has potential mercury exposure through work in a mining community and presents with psychotic symptoms

shortlist.label: Schizophrenia
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presents with hallucinations, delusions, and disorganized thinking, which are characteristic symptoms of schizophrenia

shortlist.label: Autoimmune Encephalitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presents with acute onset of psychotic symptoms and has a normal head CT scan, which could suggest an autoimmune cause

shortlist.label: Bipolar Disorder with Psychotic Features
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presents with grandiose delusions and hallucinations, which can be seen in bipolar disorder with psychotic features

raw.rationale: The patient's acute onset of psychotic symptoms, including hallucinations and delusions, in the context of a confirmed COVID-19 infection, supports this diagnosis. The absence of prior psychiatric history and the temporal relationship between the COVID-19 infection and the psychiatric symptoms further strengthen this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Mercury Poisoning
rejected.why: While the patient has potential mercury exposure, there are no specific symptoms or lab findings indicative of mercury poisoning, such as tremors, kidney damage, or characteristic lab results.

rejected.label: Schizophrenia
rejected.why: The acute onset of symptoms over one week is atypical for schizophrenia, which usually has a more gradual onset and often includes a prodromal phase.

rejected.label: Autoimmune Encephalitis
rejected.why: There is no mention of specific antibodies or inflammatory markers in the cerebrospinal fluid that would support this diagnosis, and the presentation is more consistent with a direct viral effect than an autoimmune process.

rejected.label: Bipolar Disorder with Psychotic Features
rejected.why: The absence of a prior history of mood episodes (manic or depressive) and the presence of a clear precipitating factor (COVID-19 infection) make this diagnosis less likely.
